text.what: New Zealand's most-told vine story: a cutting confiscated at Auckland airport in the 1970s, handed to a customs officer who happened to make wine, propagated, and now planted the length of the country.
text.story: *Tradition holds —* the cutting came from the Domaine de la Romanée-Conti, in a traveller's boot, and Malcolm Abel took it home. The nickname 'gumboot' is the version of the story New Zealand prefers to tell. Its origin has never been documented publicly; its behaviour in the vineyard has.

kin.as: Where it was first propagated in quantity.
And where it now grows, 900 km further south.
The practice this story sits at the edge of.
